utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning, everyone in and around the courtroom. This is case IT-08-91-T, the Prosecutor versus Mico Stanisic and Stojan Zupljanin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Good morning to everyone. May we have the appearances, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. For the Office of the Prosecutor, Gerard Dobbyn with Joanna Korner and our Case Manager, Crispian Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. For the Defence, Slobodan Zecevic, Mr. Eugene O'Sullivan, and I think you have met our expert Professor Dr. Mladen Bajagic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours, for Zupljanin Defence this morning, Igor Pantelic, Dragan Krgovic, Mr. Jason Antley, and our charming assistant Ms. Anna Wallington.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you. Would the usher please escort the witness back to the stand.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Just one second, Your Honours, I wonder if we could get the Defence expert's name again, as it wasn't picked up in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Professor Dr. Mladen Bajagic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Sorry, could you spell that, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] M-l-a-d-e-n B-a-j-a-g-i-c.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Bravo, Alpha, Juliet, Alpha, Golf, India, Charlie. Thank you very much, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You are welcome, Mr. Cvijetic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Good morning, Ms. Hanson. I remind you that you are still under oath.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Mrs. Hanson.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: When we adjourned yesterday we were discussing some issues regarding the formation and the work of region known as ARK, but now I would like to have your opinion and to pose a certain couple of questions, I would say, with regard to the other matter which is the -- to some extent the basis for the previous issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: So I would like to call, please, document, it's document on the 65 ter list 2597. It should be a document with the title "Statement of Principles for the New Constitutional Arrangements for Bosnia-Herzegovina." Yes, that's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: If you remember, Mrs. Hanson, yesterday we mentioned a number of international documents with regard to the organisation of Bosnia-Herzegovina. One amongst all these documents was so-called Cutileiro plan or Lisbon agreement. And in this particular document, I would like to outline section B in this document which is related to the general principles of how constituent units would be governed and in accordance with which principles. Would you agree with me that these general principles mentioned in section B of this document actually speak about the -- and are founded on the general principles of human rights, modern constitutional law principles and international law principles, would you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And then could we move to section E of this particular document.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: It should be page 3 English version, with the reference SA01-7150. It's E.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Now, I would like to draw your attention to the section E, which, from my point of view, speaks of the territory of the so-called units, and also speaks of other particular aspect like potential process of resolving the matter with regard to Sarajevo and also with regard to the position of the particular nation --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic, is this within the scope, this line of question, is this within the scope of the witness's expertise?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: You are sure?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: It is in regard -- it is actually with regard to the formation of Serbian municipalities and ultimately with Crisis Staff and also it is in connection with the topic of ARK, that I mentioned yesterday. So if you allow me, Your Honour, can I proceed? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Hanson, would you agree with me that the proposal in Lisbon agreement with regard to the territory division of Bosnia-Herzegovina, among other criteria, was based on the census, which means the ethnic composition of particular territory in Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see that in the English paragraph E. The B/C/S paragraph E seems to be quite a different text.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And yesterday we spoke about the development of the political system in Bosnia and Herzegovina which actually on the basis of Dayton Peace Accord divided country along the ethnic lines; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: You did ask about the Dayton Peace Agreement, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Now I would like to discuss a few issues with you with regard to the statute of the ARK that we practically left yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: It's 65 ter document 17.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Tell me, Mrs. Hanson, in your preparation of your report for this case, were you able to inspect and to check and to review a number of documents with regard to the ARK? And if yes, in short words please explain to Chamber which documents you reviewed.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I looked at the documents of the ARK Crisis Staff, the decisions, and issued an -- and orders issued by it. I did -- don't recall that I reviewed the statute of the autonomous region itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Did you, in your work, review maybe minutes or records or logs of the work of Crisis Staff of ARK?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said, I looked at the decisions. Because -- I looked also for records of other regional Crisis Staffs. Because there's such an imbalance, I felt I could not draw any conclusions about a pattern. My original tasking was to focus on the municipal level so I felt that to focus on the -- to look in depth at the ARK Crisis Staff when I don't have equivalent records from other regional Crisis Staffs would not serve the purpose of my tasking, as I understood it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: So I take from your answer that speaking of ARK in your report, aside of several decisions or conclusions, you did not review minutes, transcripts, or other documents related to the work of Crisis Staff of ARK; am I correct?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Could you tell the Chamber, please, who were the members of ARK Crisis Staff, if you can?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember them all, but I can name those who I do remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Radislav Brdjanin, Vojo Kupresanin, Momir Talic, Radisav Vukic, Sajic, Nenad Stevandic. I know I have the document in my -- one of my exhibits. I don't -- Stojan Zupljanin. That's all I can recall right now, but I can consult the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Your Honours, perhaps I could assist here. This was a document that was exhibited during her direct and it lists exactly the members that she's been asked about, so rather than having her memory tested perhaps this document can be called up. It was Exhibit P441. If this helps matters.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I absolutely agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Sorry, that's in tab 11 of your binder, Ms. Hanson. Tab 10, sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: So, Ms. Hanson, you were able to review or, let's say, to refresh your memory now, reading the list of members, yes?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: This is page 2 of this document because what we see here, it's decision regarding the general public mobilisation, so it's the next page, yes. Could you tell the Chamber, Mrs. Hanson, please, the party membership of the people, persons on this list, if you know, of course, because you are an expert of the Crisis Staff? For example, Mr. Brdjanin, he was a member of which party?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: The SDS.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Excuse me, could we have English version on the screen of this document. Because in B/C/S we have decision of the formation and ... That's correct, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And Lieutenant-Colonel Sajic, who was a vice-president, do you know his party membership?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: If he was a lieutenant-colonel in the JNA, I would assume he was a member of the League of Communists, although what that meant at this moment in May 1992 is different from what meant, say, two years earlier to be a member of the League of Communists. So I can't say for sure his affiliation. I would expect his earlier party affiliation to be League of Communists.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I take it from your answer, actually, that with regard to the vice-president of Crisis Staff, you were not able to check or to establish his party membership; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't examine that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And what about person under number 3, Mr. Kupresanin, Vojo Kupresanin --

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was a --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: -- do you know his party membership?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was a member of the Main Board of the SDS.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Under number 4, Mr. Erceg, do you know his party affiliation?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe he was SDS.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: But you don't know for sure?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't check it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: What about Mr. Radic, under number 5?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was also a member of the Main Board of the SDS.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: What about of Dr. Vukic?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was a member of the Main Board and the Executive Board of the SDS.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And Dr. Milanovic?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Below -- of the names following Vukic, I did not check the party affiliation or position of anybody, although, Nenad Stevandic, I'm pretty sure I've seen him as an SDS member, but I simply didn't look one way or another at the rest of the names.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Including my client Zupljanin, you don't know?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: So, Mrs. Hanson, in this particular case, we could not say for certain that this Crisis Staff was run established and organised exclusively by SDS party; am I correct?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the basis of this decision alone, no. On a wider understanding of the creation of the ARK and the involvement of the leadership of the SDS in its establishment and operations, one could understand the role of the SDS and the ARK. From this decision alone, we don't see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: All right. Let's speak about the role of SDS. First of all, would you agree with me that on the basis of the official election results in 1990, multi-party -- first multi-party election in Bosnia-Herzegovina, SDS won -- among the Serbian, Bosnian Serb parties, won a huge majority in terms of percentage; am I correct?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And as we discussed yesterday, in Bosnian Serb Assembly a part of duly elected SDS MPs, I think we mentioned MPs from Serbian movement of resistance --

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Renewal.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Something like SPO --

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Renewal.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: -- SPO, and couple of independent MPs; am I correct?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's my general understanding, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: So isn't it logical that the party who won, in terms of majority percentage, has a particular responsibility to act in extraordinary circumstances which, in fact, SDS did; am I correct?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: The party won the majority of the Serbian vote. It did not win the majority of the vote of Bosnia overall.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, but my question was focused specifically on Bosnian Serb institutions, so my question was directed to the role of SDS within the organs and the institution of Bosnian Serb municipalities. So, again, am I correct if I'm saying that the role of SDS was that, given the fact that they won majority of the votes, they were obliged to act and to be ready for exceptional circumstances? Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Like HDZ from Croatian side and SDA from Muslim side, because we agreed, in our previous cross-examination with Mr. Zecevic and me, that the other two national parties in Bosnia formed on a various level their Crisis Staff; am I correct?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: We saw the Presidency Crisis Staff and an HDZ Crisis Staff. I didn't see in the cross-examination an SDA Crisis Staff. But, yes, I agree that Crisis Staffs were formed on all sides.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I will -- in due course I will give you few documents with regard to this Crisis Staff. But so, okay. Let's take a look on preamble of this decision of formation of ARK Crisis Staff where it says that on the basis or pursuant to Article 12 of the Law on National Defence of Bosnian Serb Republic, this Crisis Staff was formed. That's what we see in the preamble, yes?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: In your expertise did you or were you able to take a look or check the provisions of Republika Srpska national Law on National Defence?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have looked at some of the articles.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Article 12 particularly?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't recall without being shown it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Just a second please. Could you bear with me. I have to check with my assistant.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's one of the articles of Murphy's Law when you cannot find the documents, when you will not find him. So please bear with me a second. I do apologise. We discussed this particular article, but we didn't actually download it in the e-court. So I do apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Anyhow, Mrs. Hanson, speaking of this particular basis of the establishment of Crisis Staff, would you agree with me that actually -- and I think you mentioned it earlier in your submissions, that actually the basis was -- for formation of Crisis Staff was actually in this category of national defence, am I correct? Like, you know, committees for ONO and DSZ, something like that, along these lines?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said, I have found no explicit reference to Crisis Staffs in the Law on Defence. The relevant article that Municipal Crisis Staffs sometimes cite refers simply to the organisation of defence on the territory. There's no reference that I know of, that I can recall, but I don't have a photographic memory, to committees for All People's Defence in the RS legislature, I'd be surprised to see a reference. So I don't see references to Crisis Staffs or All People's Defence committees, simply an obligation to organise defence, and Crisis Staffs are formed on that basis. I see no explicit legislative basis for Crisis Staffs and no explicit connection made in a normative document between Crisis Staffs and All People's Defence committees. I have agreed that the concept is the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Absolutely, I agree with you, and I can confirm that in Article 12, there is no -- any reference to Crisis Staff in this term, but rather, a broader basis which is a, let's say, development from previous legislation from former Yugoslavia with regard to the committee for ONO and DSZ, I agree with you. But tell me, in this particular decision, the actually, I understand it, the Executive Board of ARK Assembly, and we see the president was Mr. Nikola Erceg, actually adopted this decision of formation of Crisis Staff; am I correct?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what it states in this decision, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And would you agree with me that in ARK actually -- I mean, in accordance with your previous work on this topic, actually we got two bodies. We've got Crisis Staff of ARK and we got War Staff of ARK; am I correct?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I see them as the same body here because the title reads "Decision on the Formation of the Crisis Staff" and then it names the War Staff, so I take those terms to be interchangeable here.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Well, according to my knowledge, in fact, and I'm putting to you this fact, although you mentioned that you didn't check, I'm putting to you that Crisis Staff was actually organised and run by Mr. Brdjanin and his associates without any other official member. Do you know this fact?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that Brdjanin was the president of the Crisis Staff. I know that he was indicted and tried here. I am aware of that case. I'm not aware of the extent of his other -- of other people being excluded from the staff. I know that Talic was originally indicted and tried with him, so I know that he was not alone. I did not read into that case when I prepared for my testimony here so I'm not going to comment on the extent to which he operated alone.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And actually, the War Staff of ARK actually was a body for more, I would say -- body for focused for more other aspects of the life in terms of organisation, defence, et cetera, not actually politically, and that's why the list of -- this list of members is quite long. That is my position. Are you aware about this fact?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware that there were two bodies co-existing at the same time, the Crisis Staff and War Staff of ARK.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Okay, let's now take a look on the next page of this document, which is -- yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I see here that on the session or meeting of Crisis Staff, which was held on 8th of May, 1992, ARK Crisis Staff adopted following conclusions --

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: The decision on the board is the 6th of May. I think there's two different ones again. The English and the B/C/S are not the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, you are right. It's next -- yes, you are right.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: It's under -- English version should be under 4. This is 3, so next decision.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you for correct me, Mrs. Hanson. Yes, that's right. So here we see that the ARK Crisis Staff adopted the following conclusions, and the conclusion number 1 is that: "The presidents of the National Defence Councils are to supply detailed information to the War Staff of ARK..." So this is completely new body, I mean, related to another issue. It is not -- Crisis Staff directs, Crisis Staff of ARK directs the presidents of National Defence Councils to report to War Staff; am I correct?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what it reads here in this decision. I --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And then in paragraph 3 of the same conclusion, again ARK Crisis Staff direct presidents of the National Defence Councils to inform War Staff of ARK. And then again, under 4, we have a part of this conclusion that mass media are directed to promptly inform all citizens of the orders of War Staff. And then again, under 7 of the same conclusions, we have decision that travel agencies should be put under the control of War Staff of ARK. And then under 9, we also have a mention of War Staff. And then under 13, instead of Mr. Rajko Kuzmanovic, by the way, who is the president of Bosnia-Herzegovina now and Republika Srpska, instead of him as a War Staff, nomination was done for Dr. Mirjanic. So we see how it's function -- how it's functioning, the Crisis Staff directs to various institutions and body to report with regard to certain issues to War Staff. Is that what is said here in this decision?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what it says here.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And then we have a meeting on 9th of May. This is number 6 here in this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: This is number 6, I believe. It is ERN number 0049-7843 of the same Official Gazette. So if this is document number 4 -- you see on the top left number 4, so we have to go to the document with number, please. Yes. Okay. So we have 6 in B/C/S and we have --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: We are not going to comment into details all this documents, but I'd just like it to draw your attention to the conclusions under 1 and 2 where, for example, under 1 we have decision that media centre should be formed for needs of War Staff, and then the decision that all operative orders of War Staff should be followed. And then again, on the session of 11th of May, ARK Crisis Staff adopted a number of conclusions, whereas also there are some directions with regard to the -- to the ... Now, this is actually -- correction. Decisions -- now we have another line of work of Crisis Staff. Now we have in the -- on the session of 11th of May, we have all decisions relevant to -- to Crisis Staff. So two days before we have -- and earlier we have certain directions with regard to the War Staff, and now we have something which is strictly related to Crisis Staff. Were you able to check these two documents, please?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see the difference in the term used, yes. I see that the earlier documents within the text refer to War Staff, whereas this one within the text refers to Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Of course. And, again, you were not able to check any minutes, records, log-books of the work of War Staff or ARK Crisis Staff; am I correct?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not check any minutes, records, or log-books of either War Staff or Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: So your, I would say, assumption is expressed in your expert report, rather than expert conclusions on the basis of more profound and detailed documents; am I correct?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have explained why I did not look in depth at the ARK documents. So, yes, my conclusions as regard regional Crisis Staffs are very different as compared to those regarding Municipal Crisis Staffs. I do recall, however, the Sanski Most Crisis Staff saying that the Crisis Staff now functions as a War Staff, publicly the old name will be used. And on the basis of my reading, I would say that that is a possible interpretation of these documents as well. But I cannot draw that conclusion as regarding ARK because I'm reluctant, as I said, to draw many conclusions regarding regional Crisis Staffs.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: That was my point actually with regard to the ARK Crisis Staff. Thank you, Ms. Hanson, for your answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Just for me to be sure --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: -- in what document are we right now? In which document?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: We are -- Your Honour, we are in the document which is provided to us by our friends from the Prosecution. This is a document --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Is it 147?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Just a moment, Your Honour, please bear with me. This is 65 ter document 147. That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: So in this document, actually this is Official Gazette of ARK region where a number of decisions were adopted, published, et cetera. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And now --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: We inquired of the Registry about 15 minutes ago as to how much time you had left and at that point it was 30 minutes, so you will bear that in mind.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, time is really passing very fast especially here in Courtroom I, but, please, I was extremely -- Your Honour, I beg you for your kindness, I will almost finish, but if couple of minutes I will need, please allow me that because I just want to finish this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: That's why we thought we should alert you at this point.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Much obliged, Your Lordship.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Now, Mrs. Hanson, please, could we take a look on --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I call Exhibit P68, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I believe, Ms. Hanson, that we agreed upon the fact that region of ARK was duly formed and established in accordance with the constitution of -- Bosnia-Herzegovina constitution in September 1991 covering all this area, or maybe we are not agreed upon that fact. What is your position?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agreed that it was constituted, but I do not agree that it was necessarily established in accordance with the constitution.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I put to you a fact that on the basis and in accordance of the constitution of Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, three constituent nations through their respective MPs formed ARK region. What is your position with regard to that fact? You agree or you disagree?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not believe that the constitution --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Or you don't know?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- of Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: No, no, no, please stop, Ms. Hanson. I put to you -- you are an expert, you have to be expert. I put to you a fact, you can say, Yes, I agree, I disagree, or I don't know. Please one of these three options, and then you can clarify that in redirect. Please my question was very simply and straightforward.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Your Honours, if I could just intervene here. At the start of this cross-examination, Mr. Pantelic put it to Ms. Hanson that she was not an expert in constitutional law and she agreed with that. And now he is saying that as an expert, he demands that she answer this question about constitutional law, so it's outside the scope.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Absolutely -- well, no. No, it's a very simple question. Ms. Hanson is your expert for the work of Crisis Staff. Crisis Staff are actually derived from the municipalities from certain regions, which we are speaking here of ARK. So my question is, what is the basis of Crisis Staff of ARK. It should be in certain institutions, so this institution is ARK region. And my question was very simple. It is not to do with the constitutional law issues, with the, I don't know, international law issues, it's a simple fact, she is an expert. She know or she doesn't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Please, proceed, Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: What is your answer?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I disagree.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Please take a look on the list of deputies. It's Prosecution Exhibit, as I mentioned, 68. And could you tell me from your knowledge, because you spent a lot of time in analysing documents in Bosnia, under 12, could we agree that Mr. Sabic, Mehmed, is a Bosnian Muslim?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: The name would certainly suggest that. I don't know the man personally so I don't know how he identifies himself, but certainly it's a Muslim name.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Absolutely, I'm limited to the formulation that you just used. Absolutely. So under 27, could you agree that this gentleman Kozjan might be of Croat origin?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first name certainly suggests Croat origin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And under 31, Mr. Biscevi, Edib, being a Bosnian Muslim?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what the name would suggest.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And also under 32?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the name is Muslim.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And then under 52, Mr. Karahodzic?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's a Muslim name.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And, sorry, number 58?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's a Muslim name.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And then 86, Mrs. Sehovic?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's a Muslim name.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: So, Mrs. Hanson, I put to you that in accordance with the legislation of Bosnia and Herzegovina in 1991, a number of municipalities being a part of ARK actually gave the authority or voted for their representatives from municipality Assembly to ARK municipality. Do you agree with me or not? Or you are not informed about this process?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not believe that ARK is named in the legislation of Bosnia-Herzegovina. Therefore, I cannot agree with your statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: All right. That's your position.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: But let's go now to document 2D25.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: This document speaks about the relation between CSB Banja Luka and local police stations. First of all, Mrs. Hanson, were you able to see or to read or to check this document?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's one of my exhibits. Tab 34.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I will not go into every detail of this document, but would you agree with me that in the part, the first part of document, introductory part, so let's establish that the author of this document is the CSB Banja Luka and its chief Mr. Zupljanin; am I correct?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And it's dated on 30th of July, 1992?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: So in the first part of this document, namely from page 1 until 3, Mr. Zupljanin, of course, you don't have reason to -- not to believe me, but Mr. Zupljanin with his associates, with his services practically formulated this document, and in this first part of this document, he is speaking about certain events and certain, I would say, problems which was located in the work of local police stations; am I correct? I mean in general terms.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And then on, it's page 3 of B/C/S, Mr. Zupljanin -- it's page 3 but it's bottom of the page 3 where he states, yes. And then Mr. Zupljanin -- let's wait for the English version. Mr. Zupljanin orders very specifically under 1, he directs that all activities of local police stations must be within the provisions of the Law of Interior of Republika Srpska; am I correct?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what it says.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And then under 2 of this document, Mr. Zupljanin states that local police stations cannot take any orders or other decisions from various Crisis Staff and other organisations, which are not in accordance with the legal framework; am I correct?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And then on, at the same item, he actually outlined that the various political decisions without any legal form cannot be followed by the members of the police service; am I correct?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what it says, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And then under item 3, he directs local police chiefs and the stations that in any delicate or complicated matter they are obliged to contact CSB; is that what is the gist of item 3?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And then in number 4, he is instructing local police authorities that the professional approach with regard to the detention or arrest, in accordance with the law, without any ethnic discriminatory approach must be followed; am I correct?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's the gist of it, yes. I don't think he says exactly professional approach, but certainly the gist is to start acting in accordance with the law.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And then under 5, local police stations are obliged to, on the basis of the law, of course, perform activities with regard to the collection of information or proceedings against the persons allegedly committed certain crimes; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is what it states, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And then under 6, it's a directive to local police stations that without previous accordance or approval of CSB cannot be in the escort or give any assistance to the detained people?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: To people detained by unauthorised persons, it says.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. And then under 7, we have a directive regarding the issue of paramilitary formations and then also we have the issue that local police stations must perform investigative activities against the alleged criminal activities of paramilitary formations, and the other armed groups and individuals. Is that the gist of item number 7 in this document?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what the document seems to be saying.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And then item 8 speaks about the more technical issues like traffic issues; yes?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: It refers to checkpoints, but earlier in the text they describe some problems with checkpoints set up by people other than the police, so I don't think it's just a question of traffic issues.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Checkpoints, sorry. My mistake. Yes, we agree about checkpoints. Under item number 9, it's a direction to take immediate, decisive, and uncompromising action to throw light on all alleged criminal activities within the police stations, to take necessary disciplinary -- to launch necessary disciplinary procedures as well as criminal procedures, suspension of police officers, if any, in the accordance with the provision of the law of criminal procedure; is that the gist of item 9, Mrs. Hanson?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what it says.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And then under 10, it is necessary when these preliminary procedures will finish that all cases against members of local police stations must be forwarded to the public prosecutor; am I correct?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And under 11, that it is forbidden for the local police chiefs to, without prior approval of CSB, to make any changes in employee list; am I correct?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what it says.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And then on the next page, which is the end of this document, it's page 6 of B/C/S, and the English should be -- yes. He speaks and he directs that direct responsibility for all these orders are local chiefs of police; am I correct?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And that on the basis of previous collected informations, that this organ, being CSB, will take a very precise and concrete steps against the particular -- particular individuals; am I correct?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what it says.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And in conclusion of this document, a dead-line was imposed, which is the 10th of August, 1992, where by this date a detailed report should be submitted to CSB; am I correct?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what it says.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And in your report, in your report, it's footnote 140, page of 39 of your report, your conclusion, I am not going into details because my learned friend Mr. Zecevic covered all these matters and we know that you are not police expert and that your conclusions with regard to the provisions of law of interior are not related to this case, but what you said here, you said in footnote 140, you said: "Order from CSB Banja Luka indicates," so now you are making a conclusion, "indicates that the local police station had been accepting and carrying out orders issued by municipal and regional Crisis Staff." It is not the point. The main point of this document is that Mr. Zupljanin, as the head of CSB, actually directed all local police officers and chiefs to follow the law, to follow the order, and the principles of work, that is the spirit of this document, and you didn't mention that spirit, why? You are one-sided, you are -- or you are biased? Why? Why you didn't mention this spirit of this very important document?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree that that is the spirit of this document which is directed from the head of the centre to the local police stations, but I was looking at it from the point of view of the relations between the municipal authorities and the local police stations. And I believe that Mr. Zupljanin would not have written that item, that they have to follow procedure and not take orders from municipal and regional Crisis Staffs that don't follow proper procedure, he would not have written that had they -- the local police stations not been receiving such orders that are beyond their domain, that are not following procedure. I agree that's the thrust of the document, but I, as an analyst, I have to ask why is this document being written? Why would he write something like that? He would not write it if the police stations had not been receiving -- not been accepting irregular orders from their Crisis Staffs. I think reading this document, anyone who looks at it would certainly agree that the thrust of it is an attempt, in the end of July, to assert the -- the correct procedure and the rule of law. As I indicate in my report, you have to look at the time-period, and it's quite consistent with my conclusions that by the end of the July, the police officials are taking this stand and that he is describing problems that -- and events that have occurred up until this point.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I agree with you, you are the author of report and this is your, I would say, approach and liberty, but my point was more directed to the issue and to the aspect of objectivity as a component of independent view in the report, that was my idea. But, okay, Mrs. Hanson, let's go to our --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: It's 10.25, Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honour. Just for information, I have just a couple of questions, so in five or ten minutes, I can finish, even less. Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Welcome back, Ms. Hanson. Now I would like to just cover -- it's more or less housekeeping matters to cover some issues with regard to your testimony before the Sarajevo court.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: So could we have please, it's an e-court document, 1D01-0412. Actually, this is a transcript of Mrs. Hanson testimony before the Bosnian state court in Sarajevo in case of Mr. Klickovic, who was, I believe, president of Crisis Staff of municipality of Bosanska Krupa in 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Do you remember that testimony, Ms. Hanson?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And it was on 27th of January, 2009, and 28th of January, 2009, this year, yes?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: In transcript, you -- it is page 66 of B/C/S version -- oh, sorry, 49. And English version is 66. 49, yes. And then around last third of the page, just a moment. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: The accused, I don't know who asked you, maybe, Mr. Klickovic, but it's not important for this moment, asked you that you filed the updated version of your report of July 2008. Could you please be so kind to explain us, first of all, in this particular case, you filed your report which was specifically designed for the municipality of Bosanska Krupa, in that case in Sarajevo, or it was a kind of expanded version, could you explain that, please?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: The report which I gave to the Bosnian state court was essentially the same as this report here. I don't recall if there were a few paragraphs that might have differed, but it was -- certainly formed the basis of this -- very similar to this report. It was not at all specific to Bosanska Krupa.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: In any case, a report that you filed before the Sarajevo court in July 2008 is practically a later version of your report from February 2008; am I correct?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: There are --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Or these are completely two different reports?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, no, they are very similar reports. As I say, there were a few paragraphs where I may have re-worded things. I don't recall the essence of the differences, but it is very much the same report. With the same conclusions. The paragraphs I may have rewritten were not -- were better phrasing, not change of conclusions.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Any case, I don't believe that we --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Did we, can I ask my friends from the Prosecution, did we get this report, this updated from July 2008? No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: I am sorry, I can't say off the top of my head. I will check that and we can get back to you, if that's what you'd like.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Anyhow, Mrs. Hanson, please, the question here at this trial in Sarajevo was related to the Crisis Staff formed in Croatia in 1991, and then on the Muslim and Croatian side during the war in Bosnia, and you said yes, and I believe you stand with your answer today also on regard to this issue?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I've been shown here documents showing that they were formed before the war, so I would change that in my statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, of course, but also -- and during the war?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and during the war. I do not stand that it was only during the war now.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you for that. Just a moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Now, can we go to page -- it's page 97. Actually, this is the second day of your testimony. It was on 28th of January. Let me check with my colleague. Yeah, this is page 97 of the transcript English version. And this is page 4 of B/C/S of that particular day that we have here.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And, yes, okay, just a moment. The accused posed you a question which starts: "Are you aware that from 15 to 16 October, the Muslim Croat coalition adopted a declaration," and so on and so and so forth and then the line of this questions actually was finished with your answer which was the following. The --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Can we please go this -- can we have this page up. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Okay. This is what I'm interested in your answer. In your answer with regard to the developments and issues in Bosnian Assembly, Bosnia-Herzegovina Assembly in October 1991, you stated before the court in Sarajevo that: "These events were not pointed out; the instructions made -- instructions," I believe it's Variant A and B, "the instructions make no explicit connection, but they were, however, events which contributed to the crisis in former Yugoslavia. It is in these terms that I see the setting up of Crisis Staff of the Bosnian Serbs as part of the overall process." Do you stand by your statement that you gave before Sarajevo court today here?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I even have words from Klickovic himself that would support that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I finish with this couple issues.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And now, it's time, Mrs. Hanson, to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Sorry, I was just reading the document and it seems that there was a difference in the document and the interpretation -- or the transcript. Sorry, not the interpretation, but the transcript. We now have the document back on the screen and what I see Mrs. Hanson replying at the court in Sarajevo was the following: "These events were not pointed out; the instructions make no explicit connection. But they were, however, events which contributed to the crisis in the former Yugoslavia. It is in these terms that I see this setting up of Crisis Staffs of the Bosnian Serbs as part of the overall process." Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: So to make conclusion, in light of the overall process of the events in Bosnia and really serious situation, we could agree that the creation of Crisis Staff was sort of answer to the amount of extraordinary circumstances around all three nations in Bosnia, I would say?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was both an answer and a catalyst itself for further events.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So, Mrs. Hanson, it is time for us to reach certain conclusions with regard to your testimony. First of all, would you agree with me that on the basis of what we heard here from you that, in fact, you were not able in fully capacity to assess, review, and make conclusions with regard to the functioning of ARK Crisis Staff due to the lack of possibility to have a review in relevant documents such as minutes, records, et cetera; is that a correct conclusion?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: The phrase "was not able" is where I cannot agree. I could have -- I don't know the extent of our holdings on ARK. Did we -- if we had minutes, records beyond the decisions and conclusions, I simply don't know if I was able or not to look at them. It was the dearth of documents from the other regional Crisis Staffs that led me to say, I'm not going to look at ARK in-depth because it won't let me -- I will not be able to draw any conclusions about the overall pattern of regional Crisis Staffs. So I'm unaware of the extent of our holdings beyond the kind of decisions we've seen. Had I been tasked to look at ARK in-depth, I may have been able to look at more. I did not. The ability is what I cannot answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Would you agree with me with the conclusion that all three national leading parties in Bosnia-Herzegovina, SDS, HDZ, and SDA, formed in 1991 and 1992 their respective Crisis Staffs with the ultimate aim to function in extraordinary circumstances as a period until the time when the relevant municipality Assemblies could convene; would you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know enough about the SDA Crisis Staffs to be able to answer that. But from what I've seen of just what you've shown me or your colleagues showed me of the HDZ Crisis Staff and what I've seen of the SDS, I will agree to that extent.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And would you agree with me that it is a fact of common knowledge that Bosnian Serb institutions like Assembly, government, Municipal Assemblies, are recognised as the legitimate and lawful organs of today's entity known as Republika Srpska within the sovereign state Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina; would you agree with that fact?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, to the best of my knowledge.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And, finally, would you agree with me that in light of the position of the SDS being a leading party with majority MPs in Bosnian Serb Assembly which was formed in 1991 and being a leading party in accordance with the official election result in Bosnia-Herzegovina from 1990, that SDS tried to form Municipal Crisis Staff not exclusively with SDS member but also with the other members of other Serbian political parties? Would you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I could expand on why I don't agree, but I don't know if you want me to.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Well, the facts are speaking differently. But thank you very much, Mrs. Hanson, for your time being with us. I wish you, well, not safe trip but safe way to your Office of the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And thank you so much, Your Honour, I finish my cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Sorry, before Mr. Pantelic finishes, I just wonder if there may be something which has been omitted inadvertently. In the course of his cross-examination earlier on, he showed a document to Ms. Hanson which he said appeared to suggest that in the ARK there were two separate bodies; there was a Crisis Staff and a War Staff. And if that is his position, then it's our submission that according to Rule 90(H), he needs to actually put that to this witness as it is different to what her conclusions are, and she should be given the opportunity to respond to that. And he should put to her who he says these two separate bodies were and who were in them and if she has seen any evidence about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic, would you like to clarify this with the witness, and would you wish to tender the document into evidence?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. In fact, I will reserve my right during the Defence case because we are just, you know, following the development of Prosecution case and then we shall through witnesses and some other ways to present our position.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: No, I mean, the issue of the difference between the war commission and the Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: You mean War Staff and Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Yes, sorry, that you raised, I think you should actually finalise that matter with the witness while she's here.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Well, I will put that question to her, too.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that in ARK region practically two bodies were formed, one unofficial Crisis Staff of ARK led by Mr. Brdjanin and also the other War Staff with the completely different functions and organisation? Would you agree with this position?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: So, I think at this stage, Your Honour ...

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I am sorry, Your Honour. Can I interrupt [Realtime transcript read in error "get back to"] you? Obviously, as Your Honours know, Brdjanin was the case I dealt with. I think what needs to be made clear at this stage --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: -- is the suggestion by the Defence -- is the suggestion by the Defence that there was a totally separate body called the War Staff from the ARK Crisis Staff which was simply Mr. Brdjanin alone without any participation by Mr. Zupljanin. Is that the suggestion?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: That is my suggestion, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Right. Well, that's very clear. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: And just to clarify, Mrs. Hanson, you do not support that contention?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know enough of the case to support that. My -- my impression without having followed the case too closely is that the term that was the same body. I don't know enough to assert completely, but I've seen -- I can draw a parallel from the Sanski Most documents which said, Privately we operate as a War Staff, publicly the word "Crisis Staff" will still be used. And I think that the documents I've been shown could be interpreted parallel to that. I'm not asserting that I know definitely that they were one and the same body but I don't know enough to agree with the statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Try again, Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Okay. Would you -- I mean, I completely accept your position that you expressed earlier that you were not able to review, assess, or other way analyse relevant documents to ARK Crisis Staff, and were you able maybe through a review of certain witness statements to come to the conclusion that ARK Crisis Staff is the same like body of war Crisis Staff of ARK? As you just mentioned.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, war Crisis Staff, you mean War Staff, I did not rely on witness statements. I relied on documents from the contemporary documents, documents of the bodies concerned. I do not look at witness statements for my report.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I finish my cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic, just for the record, on page 32, line 6 in LiveNote, you asked: Would you agree with me that in ARK region practically two bodies were formed, one unofficial Crisis Staff," was it "unofficial" you said?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Well, yeah, unofficial, yes. Unofficial.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'm recorded as saying, "I'm sorry, Your Honour, can I get back to you." I don't think I said, "Can I get back to you." I rather think I said, "May I -- can I interrupt." I don't know why I would be saying, "Can I get back to you."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Re-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Good morning again, Ms. Hanson.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: In the course of the cross-examination you've faced over the last couple of days, you've had a lot of questions about the scope of your report, your expertise, what was and was not in your report. You were asked by Mr. Pantelic whether you were seen as an expert outside this particular institution and you recall saying that no, you weren't?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: He put it in terms of universities or conferences and I said no, it's true that I did testify as an expert for the Bosnian state court.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Thank you, that's what I was going to ask. Now, what exactly was the terms of reference of the report you were asked to prepare for the Krajisnik case?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not receive explicit written terms of reference for that, but my tasking was to look at the Municipal Crisis Staffs. I then -- I said, as I wrote it I realised I had to include War Presidencies and war commissions as well. So I understood my instructions to be, Look at the municipal bodies. I was asked at one point, What about the regional bodies, and I did as much as I could to look into them, and finding so little material on the regional bodies aside from ARK, I was reluctant to claim that I was also covering the regional level. So although the title of the report simply says "Crisis Staffs," the thrust is very much the municipal level.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: When you say you were asked to write a report on Municipal Crisis Staffs, was that explicitly in relation to the Municipal Crisis Staffs of one political party or one ethnic group or?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the Bosnian Serbs. It was in terms of the case against Momcilo Krajisnik and Biljana Plavsic, so it was very much Bosnian Serb Crisis Staffs.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Were you ever asked to include in the report or to look at Muslim or Croat ethnic Crisis Staffs?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Can you recall what Momcilo Krajisnik's position was during 1992?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was Speaker of the Assembly, the Bosnian Serb National Assembly, and he was a member of the expanded Wartime Presidency of the Republika Srpska as of, I believe, late May or early June 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: So that wasn't a case involving a defendant who had been a member of the Ministry of the Interior?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: It did -- however, in your first report, I believe you said you did briefly touch on the relationship between the Crisis Staffs and the police, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And you were later asked to provide an updated version of the Krajisnik report for this case; right?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: So your report was used in two different cases with two separate sets of facts. Did you alter any of your conclusions from the first report to the report for this case?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Did you alter any of the assertions that you made in the first report?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I may have refined some of my arguments, but the assertions stayed the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Now, when you expanded the section touching on the relationship between the Crisis Staffs and the police, specifically in relation to that section, did you change any of your assertions or conclusions from the Krajisnik report to this report?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Your Honours, at this time I'd like to show -- call up Ms. Hanson's Krajisnik report. It has 65 ter number 10085.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I am sorry, Your Honours, I don't believe that during the cross-examination the Krajisnik report was ever brought up. I don't know how it derives from the cross-examination that my learned friend can use it in redirect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Dobbyn, the same thing occurred to me. What -- how are you permitted to show this at this stage?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm just looking for a specific reference, but it's my recollection that it was actually -- the genesis of the present report was referred to on several occasions, and if I'm given a moment, I'll try to find a specific reference for Your Honours. Yes, Your Honours if we look at transcript page 4453, from questions from Mr. Zecevic, and this is line 10: "In the light of the Judge's questions, let me ask you one more thing. You said your first report was created on the basis of a memorandum written by you as part the Prosecution team in Krajisnik, and then the Prosecutors leading that case asked you to write it in the form of a report." Now he then goes on, Your Honour, I don't want to quote it verbatim, but saying that this basic report was amended and was adjusted and was updated for this case, so I believe it has been raised.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm not disputing this, but the point of the matter is the witness's testimony is that she only added to the report, to the existing report of Krajisnik. She only added the part referring to the minister of interior and therefore we never used the Krajisnik report in our cross-examination. We only used the report in Stanisic-Zupljanin case. And --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: But, with respect, Mr. Zecevic, aren't we spending unnecessary time on what is a really technical objection having regard to the common basis, the common nature of these reports?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I agree with Your Honour. I'm just trying to establish sort of rules in the redirect for the future. Thank you very much. That is very correct from Your Honours that it's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: We have all walked that path before, but in this case --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honour. I understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And Your Honours, I would be happy to make it clear where I'm going with these questions but I just don't think it's suitable when the witness is present, so if I can just carry on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes, proceed, Mr. Dobbyn.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Sure. So, again, if we could call up that document. That's 10085. And I'd like to look at paragraph 57. It's on page 29 of the English and page 31 of the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I am sorry, Your Honour, just one more technical question. Is this document on the 65 ter list?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Your Honours, it's not on the 65 ter list. On the basis that it has been opened by the -- sorry, this issue has been opened up by the Defence in cross-examination, I believe it's only proper for us to be able to address it. Again, I could go further with the explanation, I just don't think it's proper in the witness's presence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Again, I'm thinking of time and the significance of this. If this wasn't on your 65 ter list, need we really spend time on trying to do this?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: I take your point, Your Honours, and perhaps I'll just go back to the question I had before.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Ms. Hanson, the section on police. Am I correct in understanding that you expanded that section?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Did you change any other section that had been included in the Krajisnik report and the report that you have written in this case?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not change my basic conclusions. It became a longer section. Those are the changes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm happy to move on without getting into the prior report at this point.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Now referring to transcript page 4456 onwards, you were asked a number of questions about historical and political events that were leading up to the formation of the Crisis Staffs. As some examples, you were asked about the October proclamation of sovereignty, the Lord Carrington-led negotiations, the conference in The Hague and so on. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: It was put to you that these events should perhaps have been included in your report; do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Now, from your knowledge, do Prosecution teams in the OTP usually rely on just one expert to cover all relevant areas of their case?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: As far as these historical and political events leading up to the war in Bosnia-Herzegovina are concerned, would you expect these to be covered by someone else other than yourself?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I would.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Having had all these questions about these events put to you, do you believe now that a discussion of these events was necessary to be included in your report to an understanding of how the Bosnian Serb Crisis Staffs were formed and how they functioned?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: On Tuesday - I'm referring to transcript page 4441 at line 12 - it was put to you that in reviewing documents for your report, you only selected those documents that fit the Prosecution's case of -- theory of the case. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: You said at that time that when you found documents that went against the Prosecution, you would bring them to the Prosecutor's attention. Do you recall that answer?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Now, I'd like to just ask you to explain this a little further. Are you referring to documents specifically that undermined your report, or are you talking more generally about Rule 68 in general?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean Rule 68 in general. It's one of my taskings to bring such material to the Prosecution's attention.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Could you just perhaps expand on that little bit, exactly what this tasking is, what it involves?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it's one of our ongoing jobs. Whatever we see, material that we consider potentially Rule 68, we identify it, sometimes we participate in some system-wide searches on certain topics, but just in the course of reviewing documents, if I see something that strikes me as supporting my understanding of the Defence case or something that contradicts my understanding of the Prosecution's general theory, it's my duty to pass it on to the team lawyers.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Thank you. Just to move on, on Wednesday - and I refer to transcript page 4449 - you were asked to identify documents in your report which perhaps do not support the Prosecution's case. Do you recall being asked that?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And do you recall that at that time being asked there and then you couldn't point to any. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: First can I ask, was the Prosecution's theory of the case ever explained to you in any detail?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And at the time of preparing this report, did you know what the Defence theory of the case would be?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: So do you think you are in any position to say for certain whether any of your documents, aside from your report, are contrary to the Prosecution's case or support the Defence case?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Your Honours, at this time if we could show Exhibit P186.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Now, do you remember being shown this document yesterday, Ms. Hanson?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And I think it was put to you, and wouldn't you agree, that on its face this document appears to undermine your assertions regarding Djeric's 26 April instructions?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: It indicates that the text of the instructions were withdrawn, but as I've indicated, I have other reasons to believe that the instructions were, in fact, issued and implemented.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: You included this document in your report and a footnote, footnote 47, with an explanatory note. Why did you specifically bring this document to attention in your report?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because it's relevant. It obviously has some bearing on understanding the instructions. In fact, I think I had a much longer section explaining why -- that I am aware of this document but how I interpret it in the light of other copies of the instructions that we found. But since my basic conclusion is that the instructions were in fact issued, received and implemented, I kept it in a footnote, but I certainly want to call the attention to -- of the reader to the fact of the existence of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Thank you. Now apart from this document or any other document -- actually if I just go back for one second. Were you ever asked to remove any document from your report because it was damaging to the Prosecution's theory of the case.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Never.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Did you do that on your own accord?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And to move on, at transcript page 4463, do you remember being asked whether you had only looked at documentary evidence for those municipalities contained in the indictment? Do you remember that being put to you?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall that question per se but I've been asked a lot of questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: If we could call up Ms. Hanson's report. That's P434, marked for identification. I'd like to go to page 25 in the English, page 26 in the B/C/S. And sorry, if we could scroll down, it's the footnotes that I'm interested in.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Ms. Hanson, the municipalities that are in bold, what does that indicate?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I bold the -- just for ease of reading I bold the name of the municipality and many of these ones here on this page are not -- as far as I know, not part of the indictment.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Could you just quickly perhaps read the names in bold, the municipalities in bold?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Bosanski Novi, Bratunac, Kotor Varos, Novo Sarajevo, Rogatica, Sanski Most, Sipovo, Bosanska Krupa, Kljuc, Bihac, Bosanski Samac.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Thank you. On Wednesday, transcript page 4463, you were asked if all SDS Municipal Boards set up Crisis Staffs in 1992, and you responded that you couldn't claim that because they're municipalities for which the OTP has no documentary evidence. Do you recall that exchange?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Now, from the documentation that you were able to review, was -- would you say that the formation of SDS Crisis Staffs was an isolated phenomenon?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Isolated in what --

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: That it only happened in a few municipalities or was it widespread?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was widespread.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: On Wednesday, again, you were asked about the secrecy or otherwise of the Variant A and B instructions, and you were shown one example, document from Zvornik, this is Exhibit P437, where it appeared that the instructions may not have been kept secret; do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Could we show Exhibit P438.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Ms. Hanson, this is in tab 5 of your binder.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And if we can go to page 306 in the English and page 278 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Ms. Hanson, we have looked at this already, but could you perhaps direct us -- sorry, I'll just wait for the correct page to come up. Could you tell us how Radovan Karadzic himself characterised these instructions, if at all, on this page?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he says: "In the municipalities where we were a minority, we formed a secret government Municipal Board, Municipal Assembly, president of the Executive Board. You remember A and B variants."

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
